D.6.4 Appeal Procedure Rules

D.6.4.1 Right to Appeal

Rule D.6.12 (Right to Appeal)

Any subject affected by an assessment result has the right to lodge an appeal.

$$\forall x: \text{AffectedBy}(x, \text{Assessment}) \Rightarrow \text{RightToAppeal}(x)$$

D.6.4.2 Appeal Procedure

Rule D.6.13 (Appeal Procedure)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Appeal Procedure                                                │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Phase 1: Appeal submission                                      │
│  ├─ Submit a written appeal                                    │  
│  ├─ State the grounds for the appeal                           │  
│  └─ Provide supporting evidence                                │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Phase 2: Preliminary review                                     │
│  ├─ Confirm the standing to appeal                             │  
│  ├─ Assess the grounds for the appeal                          │  
│  └─ Decide whether to accept the appeal                        │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Phase 3: Substantive review                                     │
│  ├─ Review the original assessment process                     │  
│  ├─ Review the grounds for the appeal                          │  
│  └─ Reassess when necessary                                    │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Phase 4: Decision                                               │
│  ├─ Uphold the original assessment                             │  
│  ├─ Modify the assessment result                               │  
│  └─ Require reassessment                                       │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Phase 5: Enforcement                                            │
│  ├─ Enforce the decision                                       │  
│  └─ Record the outcome of the appeal                           │  
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

D.6.4.3 Appeal Time Limits

Rule D.6.14 (Appeal Time Limits)

PhaseTime Limit
Submission of appealWithin 30 days after the assessment result is published
Preliminary reviewWithin 14 days after receiving the appeal
Substantive reviewWithin 60 days after acceptance
Enforcement of decisionWithin 14 days after the decision

D.6.5 L₄ Layer Revision Procedure

D.6.5.1 Conditions for Revision

Rule D.6.15 (L₄ Revision Conditions)

L₄-layer revisions are initiated under the following conditions:

ConditionDescription
Operational problemsThe procedure encounters problems in operation
Efficiency problemsThe procedure is insufficiently efficient
User feedbackImprovement suggestions are received from users
Technological progressTechnological progress permits a better method
Upper-layer changeA revision of the L₃ layer requires an adjustment of the L₄ layer

D.6.5.2 Revision Procedure

Rule D.6.16 (L₄ Revision Procedure)

The L₄-layer revision procedure is the most simplified:

  1. Put forward a revision proposal
  2. Consistency check
  3. Pilot testing (if needed)
  4. PSMC approval
  5. Implementation and monitoring

D.7 Cross-Layer Consistency Rules

D.7.1 Consistency Check Procedure

D.7.1.1 Definition of Consistency

Rule D.7.1 (Definition of Consistency)

$$\text{Consistent}(L_i, L_j) \Leftrightarrow \neg \exists r_i \in L_i, r_j \in L_j: \text{Contradiction}(r_i, r_j)$$

D.7.1.2 Consistency Check Procedure

Rule D.7.2 (Consistency Check Procedure)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Consistency Check Procedure                                     │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 1: Identify the scope of the check                         │
│  ├─ Determine the layers that need to be checked               │  
│  └─ Determine the rules that need to be checked                │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 2: Perform the check                                       │
│  ├─ Compare the rules pairwise                                 │  
│  ├─ Identify potential conflicts                               │  
│  └─ Record the check results                                   │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 3: Conflict analysis                                       │
│  ├─ Confirm whether the conflict is real                       │  
│  ├─ Analyze the nature of the conflict                         │  
│  └─ Determine the severity of the conflict                     │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 4: Reporting                                               │
│  ├─ Generate a consistency-check report                        │  
│  └─ Submit it to the PSMC                                      │  
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

D.7.1.3 Periodic Checks

Rule D.7.3 (Periodic Checks)

Type of CheckFrequency
Complete checkOnce a year
Partial checkAfter each revision
Triggered checkWhen potential problems are found

D.7.2 Conflict Identification Procedure

D.7.2.1 Types of Conflict

Rule D.7.4 (Types of Conflict)

Type of ConflictDescription
Direct contradictionTwo rules directly contradict each other
Implicit contradictionThe implicit consequences of two rules contradict each other
Application conflictThe rules conflict in a specific application
Priority conflictMultiple rules apply but yield different conclusions

D.7.2.2 Conflict Identification Procedure

Rule D.7.5 (Conflict Identification Procedure)

  1. Systematically review the rules of each layer
  2. Analyze the logical relations among the rules
  3. Identify potential points of conflict
  4. Verify the reality of the conflicts
  5. Record and classify the conflicts

D.7.3 Conflict Resolution Procedure

D.7.3.1 Principles of Conflict Resolution

Rule D.7.6 (Principles of Conflict Resolution)

PrincipleDescription
Layer principleLower-layer rules take priority over upper-layer rules
Specificity principleSpecific rules take priority over general rules
Later-law principleLater-revised rules take priority (within the same layer)
Minimal revisionGive priority to the minimal-revision option

D.7.3.2 Conflict Resolution Procedure

Rule D.7.7 (Conflict Resolution Procedure)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Conflict Resolution Procedure                                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 1: Conflict analysis                                       │
│  ├─ Confirm the nature and scope of the conflict               │  
│  └─ Analyze the root cause of the conflict                     │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 2: Apply the resolution principles                         │
│  ├─ Try to apply the layer principle                           │  
│  ├─ Try to apply the specificity principle                     │  
│  └─ Try to apply the later-law principle                       │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 3: Develop solutions                                       │
│  ├─ Develop possible solutions                                 │  
│  ├─ Assess the impact of each solution                         │  
│  └─ Choose the optimal solution                                │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 4: Implement the solution                                  │
│  ├─ Revise the relevant rules                                  │  
│  ├─ Update the version number                                  │  
│  └─ Notify the relevant parties                                │  
│                                                                 │ 
│  Step 5: Verification                                            │
│  ├─ Verify whether the conflict has been resolved              │  
│  └─ Verify whether new conflicts have been introduced          │  
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

D.7.4.1 Rollback Trigger Conditions

Rule D.7.8 (Rollback Trigger Conditions)

A rollback is triggered under the following conditions:

ConditionDescription
Serious defectA serious defect is found in the new version
Consistency breakdownThe new version breaks the consistency of the protocol stack
Practical failureThe new version fails in practice
EmergencyEmergency restoration to a stable version is needed

Simulation Model Technical DocumentationAppendix E

I. The Task and Positioning of This Appendix

This appendix provides the complete technical documentation of the simulation models for The Normative Foundations of Interstellar Civilization. Simulation is the key method by which this work converts its theoretical framework into a computable, verifiable form. The task of this appendix is to provide technical specifications detailed enough to enable researchers to reproduce, extend, and critique the simulation research of this work.

II. The Relationship Between Simulation and the New Three Views

The design of the simulation models directly embodies the core ideas of the New Three Views:

E.1 General Introduction to Simulation Methodology

E.1.1 The Role of Simulation in This Work

E.1.1.1 Definition of Simulation

Definition E.1.1 (Simulation)

$$\text{Simulation} \triangleq \text{ComputationalModel}(\text{Theory}) \rightarrow \text{VirtualExperiment}$$

Simulation is the method of converting a theoretical model into a computational model and conducting experiments in a virtual environment.

E.1.1.2 Functions of Simulation in This Work

Rule E.1.1 (Simulation Functions)

Simulation performs the following functions in this work:

FunctionDescriptionCorresponding Chapter
Theoretical verificationVerify the internal consistency of theoretical assumptionsPart V
Scenario explorationExplore the theoretical performance under extreme scenariosChapters 22-27
Indicator calibrationCalibrate and validate the indicator systemPart II
Institutional simulationSimulate the operation of institutional designsPart IV
Uncertainty quantificationQuantify the impact of deep uncertaintyThroughout the book

Formal Statement

$$\text{SimulationRole} = \{\text{Verification}, \text{Exploration}, \text{Calibration}, \text{Simulation}, \text{Quantification}\}$$

E.1.1.3 The Relationship Between Simulation and Theory

Rule E.1.2 (Simulation-Theory Relationship)

Simulation does not replace theoretical argumentation but supplements it.

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  The Relationship Between Simulation and Theory                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Theoretical framework (L₁-L₂)                                   │
│       │                                                         │ 
│       │ Formalization                                           │ 
│       ▼                                                         │ 
│  Computational model                                            │ 
│       │                                                         │ 
│       │ Simulation run                                          │ 
│       ▼                                                         │ 
│  Simulation results                                             │ 
│       │                                                         │ 
│       │ Feedback                                                │ 
│       ▼                                                         │ 
│  Theoretical revision (if needed)                               │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Key constraints:                                               │ 
│  - Simulation results cannot prove a theory correct             │ 
│  - Simulation results can reveal internal problems of a theory  │ 
│  - Simulation results are constrained by model assumptions      │ 
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

E.1.1.4 The Epistemological Status of Simulation

Rule E.1.3 (Simulation Epistemology)

The epistemological status of simulation results is subject to the following constraints:

ConstraintDescription
Model dependenceSimulation results depend on model assumptions
Parameter sensitivitySimulation results are sensitive to parameter settings
Non-extrapolabilitySimulation results cannot be directly extrapolated to reality
Exploratory natureSimulation results are exploratory, not definitive

Formal Statement

$$\text{SimulationResult} = f(\text{Model}, \text{Parameters}, \text{InitialConditions})$$

$$\text{Validity}(\text{SimulationResult}) \leq \text{Validity}(\text{Model})$$

E.1.3.3 Norms for Interpreting Results

Rule E.1.9 (Norms for Interpreting Results)

The interpretation of simulation results follows these norms:

  1. Conditional statement: All conclusions are premised on "under the assumptions of this model"
  2. Uncertainty reporting: Report the uncertainty range of the results
  3. Sensitivity analysis: Report the sensitivity of key parameters
  4. Limitation statement: Explicitly state the limitations of the results

Formal Statement

$$\text{InterpretedResult} = \langle \text{Result}, \text{Conditions}, \text{Uncertainty}, \text{Sensitivity}, \text{Limitations} \rangle$$

│  Input: Environment state E_t, neighbor states {N_t}             │                    
│  Output: Perceived state P_t                                    │                     
│                                                                 │                     
│  P_t = Perceive(E_t, {N_t}, noise)                              │                     
│                                                                 │                     
│  Where:                                                         │                     
│  - Perception is affected by UCS: higher UCS → more accurate perception │             
│  - Perception is affected by network position: central position → broader perception │
│  - Perception contains noise: noise ~ N(0, σ_perception)        │                     
│                                                                 │                     
│  Formalization:                                                 │                     
│  P_t = α·E_t + β·∑(w_i·N_i,t) + ε                               │                     
│  where α, β are determined by UCS and network position          │                     
│                                                                 │                     
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Decision Rules (Decision)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Decision Rules                                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Input: Perceived state P_t, internal state S_t, goal G          │
│  Output: Action choice A_t                                      │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  A_t = Decide(P_t, S_t, G, norms)                               │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Factors considered in decision-making:                         │ 
│  1. Goal satisfaction: max U(outcome)                           │ 
│  2. Norm compliance: conform(norms)                             │ 
│  3. Resource constraint: resources ≥ cost(A)                    │ 
│  4. Reversibility preference: prefer reversible actions         │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Decision function:                                             │ 
│  A_t = argmax_a [U(a) + λ·NormScore(a) - μ·Cost(a)             │  
│                  + ν·Reversibility(a)]                          │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  where λ, μ, ν are weight parameters                            │ 
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Action Rules (Action)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Action Rules                                                    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Input: Action choice A_t                                       │ 
│  Output: State change ΔS, environmental change ΔE               │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  (ΔS, ΔE) = Execute(A_t, S_t, E_t)                              │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Action types:                                                  │ 
│  - ResourceAction: resource acquisition/consumption/transfer    │ 
│  - SocialAction: establish/break/modify social relations        │ 
│  - NormAction: adopt/violate/propose norms                      │ 
│  - CommunicateAction: send/receive information                  │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Action consequences:                                           │ 
│  - Resource change: resources += Δresources                     │ 
│  - Relationship change: neighbors updated                       │ 
│  - Norm change: norms_adopted updated                           │ 
│  - Reputation change: CRV updated                               │ 
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Learning Rules (Learning)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Learning Rules                                                  │       
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │        
│  Input: Action A_t, outcome O_t, history H                       │       
│  Output: Updated strategy π', updated belief B'                  │       
│                                                                 │        
│  (π', B') = Learn(A_t, O_t, H)                                  │        
│                                                                 │        
│  Learning mechanisms:                                           │        
│  1. Reinforcement learning: adjust action preferences based on outcomes │
│     Q(s,a) ← Q(s,a) + α·[R + γ·max Q(s',a') - Q(s,a)]          │         
│                                                                 │        
│  2. Social learning: imitate successful neighbors               │        
│     if U(neighbor) > U(self):                                   │        
│         π ← (1-β)·π + β·π_neighbor                              │        
│                                                                 │        
│  3. Norm internalization: successful norms are internalized     │        
│     if NormSuccess(n) > θ:                                      │        
│         internalize(n)                                          │        
│                                                                 │        
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

E.2.3 Environment Design

E.2.3.1 Environment Structure

Definition E.2.5 (Environment)

$$\text{Environment} = \langle \text{Space}, \text{Resources}, \text{Dynamics}, \text{Perturbations} \rangle$$

Spatial Structure

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Spatial Structure Design                                        │                   
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │                    
│  Network types (configurable):                                  │                    
│                                                                 │                    
│  1. Small-world network (Watts-Strogatz)                        │                    
│     - High clustering, short paths                              │                    
│     - Parameters: n (number of nodes), k (average degree), p (rewiring probability) │
│                                                                 │                    
│  2. Scale-free network (Barabási-Albert)                        │                    
│     - Power-law degree distribution                             │                    
│     - Parameters: n (number of nodes), m (number of connections of new nodes) │      
│                                                                 │                    
│  3. Random network (Erdős-Rényi)                                │                    
│     - Poisson degree distribution                               │                    
│     - Parameters: n (number of nodes), p (connection probability) │                  
│                                                                 │                    
│  4. Multi-layer network                                         │                    
│     - Coexistence of multiple relationship types                │                    
│     - Layers: economic, political, cultural, technological      │                    
│                                                                 │                    
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Resource System

python class ResourceSystem: """Resource system design (embodying the Negentropy Responsibility Principle)"""

Resource types resource_types = { 'energy': { energy resource 'regeneration_rate': 0.01, regeneration rate 'depletion_rate': 0.05, depletion rate 'capacity': 1000 capacity }, 'information': { information resource 'regeneration_rate': 0.1, 'depletion_rate': 0.01, 'capacity': float('inf') }, 'complexity': { complexity resource (negentropy) 'regeneration_rate': 0.001, 'depletion_rate': 0.1, 'capacity': 100 } }

Resource dynamics def update_resources(self, t): """ dR/dt = regeneration - consumption - entropy_cost """ for r_type, r_params in self.resource_types.items(): dR = (r_params['regeneration_rate'] (r_params['capacity'] - self.R[r_type])

  • self.consumption[r_type]
  • self.entropy_cost)

self.R[r_type] += dR self.dt

E.2.3.2 Environmental Dynamics

Rule E.2.3 (Environmental Dynamics)

The environment state evolves according to the following dynamics:

$$\frac{dE}{dt} = f(E, \text{AgentActions}, \text{ExternalForces})$$

Specific Equations

VariableDynamical EquationDescription
Total resources$\frac{dR}{dt} = r(K-R) - \sum c_i$Resource regeneration and consumption
Complexity$\frac{dC}{dt} = \alpha \cdot I - \beta \cdot E$Information input and entropy increase
Connectivity$\frac{d\kappa}{dt} = f(\text{interactions})$Network evolution

E.2.4 Interaction Rules

E.2.4.1 Interaction Types

Definition E.2.6 (Interaction Types)

Table E.2.3 Detailed Definition of Interaction Types

Interaction TypeDescriptionParticipantsResult
CooperationCooperative action2+Mutual benefit
CompetitionCompetitive action2+One gains, one loses
CommunicationInformation exchange2+Information update

E.2.4.2 Interaction Mechanisms

Cooperation Mechanism

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Cooperation Mechanism                                           │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Condition check:                                               │ 
│  cooperate(i, j) ← (CRV_i > θ_trust) ∧ (CRV_j > θ_trust)        │ 
│                    ∧ (expected_benefit > expected_cost)          │
│                                                                 │ 
│  Benefit calculation:                                           │ 
│  benefit(i, j) = synergy(i, j) - cost(i, j)                     │ 
│  synergy(i, j) = α·min(resources_i, resources_j)                │ 
│                  + β·complementarity(i, j)                      │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Reputation update:                                             │ 
│  if cooperate_success:                                          │ 
│      CRV_i ← CRV_i + Δ_success                                  │ 
│      CRV_j ← CRV_j + Δ_success                                  │ 
│  if cooperate_defect:                                           │ 
│      CRV_defector ← CRV_defector - Δ_defect                     │ 
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Norm Deliberation Mechanism

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Norm Deliberation Mechanism (embodying NK-4 deliberativeness)   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │ 
│  Deliberation process:                                          │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  1. Proposal stage                                              │ 
│     agent_i proposes norm_n                                     │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  2. Evaluation stage                                            │ 
│     for each agent_j in community:                              │ 
│         score_j = evaluate(norm_n, beliefs_j, interests_j)      │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  3. Voting stage                                                │ 
│     vote_j = 1 if score_j > θ_accept else 0                     │ 
│     total_support = Σ(vote_j · weight_j)                        │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  4. Adoption stage                                              │ 
│     if total_support > θ_adoption:                              │ 
│         community.adopt(norm_n)                                 │ 
│     else:                                                       │ 
│         norm_n.modify() or norm_n.reject()                      │ 
│                                                                 │ 
│  Weight calculation:                                            │ 
│  weight_j = f(UCS_j, resources_j, network_centrality_j)         │ 
│                                                                 │ 
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Core Class Implementations

python agents/base_agent.py from mesa import Agent from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import List, Dict, Optional import numpy as np

@dataclass class AgentState: """Agent state data class""" UCS: float Universal Consciousness Scale RFD: float Recursive Freedom Degree CRV: float Commitment-Verification Ratio resources: float Resources norms_adopted: List[str] Adopted norms

class BaseAgent(Agent): """ Base agent class

Embodying the core ideas of the New Three Views:

  • NC-1: Attributes are determined by network relations
  • NL-3: Consciousness and subjecthood are degree-based
  • NK-1: Cognition is participatory

"""

def __init__(self, unique_id: int, model, agent_type: str, initial_state: Optional[AgentState] = None): super().__init__(unique_id, model) self.agent_type = agent_type

Initialize state if initial_state: self.state = initial_state else: self.state = self._initialize_state()

History records self.history: List[AgentState] = []

Behavioral parameters self.learning_rate = 0.1 self.cooperation_threshold = 0.5 self.norm_adoption_threshold = 0.6

def _initialize_state(self) -> AgentState: """Initialize agent state""" return AgentState( UCS=np.random.uniform(0.3, 0.7), RFD=np.random.uniform(-0.3, 0.3), CRV=np.random.uniform(0.4, 0.8), resources=np.random.uniform(10, 100), norms_adopted=[] )

def step(self): """Single-step execution of the agent"""

  1. Perception

perception = self.perceive()

  1. Decision

action = self.decide(perception)

  1. Execution

result = self.execute(action)

  1. Learning

self.learn(action, result)

  1. Record history

self.history.append(self.state)

def perceive(self) -> Dict: """Perceive environment and neighbors""" neighbors = self.model.grid.get_neighbors( self.pos, moore=True, include_center=False )

return { 'environment': self.model.get_environment_state(), 'neighbors': [n.state for n in neighbors], 'self': self.state }

def decide(self, perception: Dict) -> str: """Decision function (subclasses implement specific logic)""" raise NotImplementedError

def execute(self, action: str) -> Dict: """Execute action""" raise NotImplementedError

def learn(self, action: str, result: Dict): """Learning update""" Reinforcement learning update reward = result.get('reward', 0) self.update_strategy(action, reward)

Social learning if result.get('observe_neighbor'): self.social_learning(result['neighbor_strategy'])

def update_strategy(self, action: str, reward: float): """Update strategy""" Q-learning update logic pass

def social_learning(self, neighbor_strategy): """Social learning""" Imitate successful neighbors pass

python model/interstellar_model.py from mesa import Model from mesa.time import RandomActivation from mesa.datacollection import DataCollector from mesa.space import NetworkGrid import networkx as nx from typing import Dict, List, Optional

class InterstellarModel(Model): """ Main model for interstellar civilization simulation

Embodying the layered design of the protocol stack:

  • L₀: Physical constraints realized through the resource system
  • L₁: New Three Views realized through agent design
  • L₂: Normative principles realized through the norm system
  • L₃: Institutional design realized through interaction rules
  • L₄: Operational indicators realized through output collection

"""

def __init__(self, config: Dict): super().__init__()

Load configuration self.config = config self.num_agents = config.get('num_agents', 100) self.network_type = config.get('network_type', 'small_world')

Create network self.network = self._create_network() self.grid = NetworkGrid(self.network)

Create scheduler self.schedule = RandomActivation(self)

Initialize resource system self.resource_system = ResourceSystem(config.get('resources', {}))

Initialize norm system self.norm_system = NormSystem(config.get('norms', {}))

Create agents self._create_agents()

Data collector self.datacollector = DataCollector( model_reporters={ 'mean_UCS': lambda m: np.mean([a.state.UCS for a in m.schedule.agents]), 'mean_RFD': lambda m: np.mean([a.state.RFD for a in m.schedule.agents]), 'mean_CRV': lambda m: np.mean([a.state.CRV for a in m.schedule.agents]), 'total_resources': lambda m: sum(a.state.resources for a in m.schedule.agents), 'norm_convergence': lambda m: m.norm_system.get_convergence(), 'gini_coefficient': lambda m: self._compute_gini() }, agent_reporters={ 'UCS': 'state.UCS', 'RFD': 'state.RFD', 'CRV': 'state.CRV', 'resources': 'state.resources' } )

Run counter self.step_count = 0 self.cooperation_count = 0 self.defection_count = 0

def _create_network(self) -> nx.Graph: """Create network structure""" n = self.num_agents

if self.network_type == 'small_world': k = self.config.get('network_k', 4) p = self.config.get('network_p', 0.1) return nx.watts_strogatz_graph(n, k, p)

elif self.network_type == 'scale_free': m = self.config.get('network_m', 2) return nx.barabasi_albert_graph(n, m)

elif self.network_type == 'random': p = self.config.get('network_p', 0.1) return nx.erdos_renyi_graph(n, p)

else: raise ValueError(f"Unknown network type: {self.network_type}")

def _create_agents(self): """Create agents""" agent_distribution = self.config.get('agent_distribution', { 'Human': 0.6, 'AI': 0.2, 'Hybrid': 0.1, 'Collective': 0.05, 'Environment': 0.05 })

for i in range(self.num_agents): agent_type = self._sample_agent_type(agent_distribution) agent = self._create_agent_by_type(i, agent_type) self.schedule.add(agent) self.grid.place_agent(agent, i)

def step(self): """Single-step execution of the model""" Collect data self.datacollector.collect(self)

Update environment self.resource_system.update()

Agent actions self.schedule.step()

Norm evolution self.norm_system.evolve(self.schedule.agents)

Update counter self.step_count += 1

def run(self, steps: int): """Run simulation""" for _ in range(steps): self.step()

return self.datacollector.get_model_vars_dataframe()

E.3 System Dynamics Model (SD)

E.3.1 Model Purpose and Scope

E.3.1.1 Model Purpose

Definition E.3.1 (SD Purpose)

$$\text{SD Purpose} = \text{FeedbackDynamics}(\text{Stocks}, \text{Flows}, t)$$

The purpose of the system dynamics model is to analyze the long-term dynamic behavior of feedback systems.

Specific Purposes

PurposeDescription

E.3.2 Stock Definitions

E.3.2.1 Core Stocks

Definition E.3.2 (Stock)

A stock is the accumulated state of the system at a given moment.

$$\text{Stocks} = \{S_1, S_2, ..., S_n\}$$

Table E.3.1 Core Stock Definitions

StockSymbolUnitDefinitionRelationship with the New Three Views
Total UCS$S_{UCS}$DimensionlessSystem total consciousness levelNL-3
Total RFD$S_{RFD}$Possibility unitsSystem possibility spaceRFP
Total CRV$S_{CRV}$Trust unitsSystem trust stockNK-4
Total resources$S_R$Negentropy unitsTotal available resourcesNL-2
Complexity$S_C$Complexity unitsSystem complexityNC-2
Norm density$S_N$Norm unitsNumber of effective normsL₂
Knowledge stock$S_K$Information unitsAccumulated knowledgeNK-2

E.3.2.2 Stock Equations

Rule E.3.2 (Stock Equations)

The change of each stock is determined by inflows and outflows:

$$\frac{dS_i}{dt} = \sum \text{Inflows}_i - \sum \text{Outflows}_i$$

Specific Equations

StockDifferential Equation
$S_{UCS}$$\frac{dS_{UCS}}{dt} = F_{UCS,in} - F_{UCS,out}$
$S_{RFD}$$\frac{dS_{RFD}}{dt} = F_{RFD,gen} - F_{RFD,red}$
$S_R$$\frac{dS_R}{dt} = F_{R,regen} - F_{R,consume}$
$S_C$$\frac{dS_C}{dt} = F_{C,create} - F_{C,entropy}$
$S_N$$\frac{dS_N}{dt} = F_{N,adopt} - F_{N,decay}$

E.3.3 Flow Definitions

E.3.3.1 Flow Types

Definition E.3.3 (Flow)

A flow is the rate of change of a stock.

$$\text{Flow} = f(\text{Stocks}, \text{Auxiliaries}, \text{Parameters})$$

Table E.3.2 Flow Definitions

FlowSymbolUnitDefinition
UCS growth$F_{UCS,in}$UCS/yearIncrease in consciousness level
UCS decay$F_{UCS,out}$UCS/yearDecrease in consciousness level
RFD generation$F_{RFD,gen}$RFD/yearExpansion of the possibility space
RFD reduction$F_{RFD,red}$RFD/yearContraction of the possibility space
Resource regeneration$F_{R,regen}$R/yearNatural recovery of resources
Resource consumption$F_{R,consume}$R/yearResource consumption through use
Complexity creation$F_{C,create}$C/yearIncrease in complexity
Entropy increase$F_{C,entropy}$C/yearComplexity loss through entropy increase

E.3.3.2 Flow Equations

Rule E.3.3 (Flow Equations)

FlowEquationParameters
$F_{UCS,in}$$\alpha_{UCS} \cdot S_K \cdot (1 - \frac{S_{UCS}}{K_{UCS}})$α_UCS, K_UCS
$F_{UCS,out}$$\beta_{UCS} \cdot S_{UCS} \cdot (1 - \frac{S_R}{R_{min}})$β_UCS, R_min
$F_{RFD,gen}$$\alpha_{RFD} \cdot S_{UCS} \cdot S_C$α_RFD
$F_{RFD,red}$$\beta_{RFD} \cdot \text{IrreversibleActions}$β_RFD
$F_{R,regen}$$r \cdot S_R \cdot (1 - \frac{S_R}{K_R})$r, K_R
$F_{R,consume}$$c \cdot S_{UCS} \cdot \text{ActivityLevel}$c
$F_{C,create}$$\alpha_C \cdot S_K \cdot S_R$α_C
$F_{C,entropy}$$\beta_C \cdot S_C$β_C

E.3.4 Auxiliary Variable Definitions

E.3.4.1 Auxiliary Variable List

Definition E.3.4 (Auxiliary Variable)

An auxiliary variable is an intermediate variable computed from stocks and parameters.

Table E.3.3 Auxiliary Variable Definitions

Auxiliary VariableSymbolCalculation FormulaDescription
Activity level$A$$f(S_{UCS}, S_R)$Degree of system activity
Norm compliance rate$NC$$\frac{S_N \cdot S_{CRV}}{S_N + k}$Proportion of norms complied with
Resource efficiency$RE$$\frac{\text{Output}}{S_R}$Resource utilization efficiency

E.3.4.2 Auxiliary Variable Equations

python Auxiliary variable computation function def compute_auxiliaries(stocks, params): """Compute auxiliary variables"""

Activity level A = stocks['S_UCS'] (stocks['S_R'] / (stocks['S_R'] + params['R_half']))

Norm compliance rate NC = (stocks['S_N'] stocks['S_CRV']) / (stocks['S_N'] + params['k_norm'])

Resource efficiency RE = (params['base_efficiency'] stocks['S_K']) / (1 + stocks['S_K'] params['diminishing_factor'])

System resilience Res = (stocks['S_C'] params['alpha_res']) \ (stocks['S_R'] params['beta_res']) \ (stocks['S_RFD'] params['gamma_res'])

Sustainability index SI = (stocks['S_RFD'] stocks['S_R']) / (stocks['S_R'] + params['R_min'])

return { 'A': A, 'NC': NC, 'RE': RE, 'Res': Res, 'SI': SI }

python sd_model/interstellar_sd.py import numpy as np from scipy.integrate import odeint from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Dict, List, Callable

@dataclass class SDState: """System dynamics state""" S_UCS: float Total UCS S_RFD: float Total RFD S_CRV: float Total CRV S_R: float Total resources S_C: float Complexity S_N: float Norm density S_K: float Knowledge stock

class InterstellarSD: """ System dynamics model of interstellar civilization

Realizing the macro dynamics of the protocol stack:

  • Resource-negentropy dynamics (corresponding to L₀ and NL-2)
  • Complexity evolution (corresponding to NC-2)
  • Norm diffusion (corresponding to L₂)

"""

def __init__(self, params: Dict): self.params = params self.state_names = ['S_UCS', 'S_RFD', 'S_CRV', 'S_R', 'S_C', 'S_N', 'S_K']

def derivatives(self, y: np.ndarray, t: float, policy: Callable = None) -> np.ndarray: """ Compute the derivatives of state variables

dy/dt = f(y, t, policy) """ Unpack state variables S_UCS, S_RFD, S_CRV, S_R, S_C, S_N, S_K = y

Compute auxiliary variables A = S_UCS (S_R / (S_R + self.params['R_half'])) NC = (S_N S_CRV) / (S_N + self.params['k_norm']) RE = (self.params['base_efficiency'] S_K) / \ (1 + S_K self.params['diminishing_factor'])

Apply policy (if any) if policy: policy_effects = policy(y, t) else: policy_effects = {}

Compute flows UCS dynamics F_UCS_in = (self.params['alpha_UCS'] S_K (1 - S_UCS / self.params['K_UCS'])) F_UCS_out = (self.params['beta_UCS'] S_UCS max(0, 1 - S_R / self.params['R_min'])) dS_UCS = F_UCS_in - F_UCS_out

RFD dynamics F_RFD_gen = self.params['alpha_RFD'] S_UCS S_C NC F_RFD_red = self.params['beta_RFD'] A (1 - NC) dS_RFD = F_RFD_gen - F_RFD_red

CRV dynamics F_CRV_build = self.params['alpha_CRV'] NC S_UCS F_CRV_decay = self.params['beta_CRV'] S_CRV (1 - NC) dS_CRV = F_CRV_build - F_CRV_decay

Resource dynamics F_R_regen = self.params['r'] S_R (1 - S_R / self.params['K_R']) F_R_consume = self.params['c'] A S_UCS dS_R = F_R_regen - F_R_consume

Complexity dynamics F_C_create = self.params['alpha_C'] S_K S_R RE F_C_entropy = self.params['beta_C'] S_C dS_C = F_C_create - F_C_entropy

Norm dynamics F_N_adopt = self.params['alpha_N'] S_UCS (1 - S_N / self.params['K_N']) F_N_decay = self.params['beta_N'] S_N (1 - S_CRV) dS_N = F_N_adopt - F_N_decay

Knowledge dynamics F_K_learn = self.params['alpha_K'] S_UCS A (1 - S_K / self.params['K_K']) F_K_forget = self.params['beta_K'] S_K (1 - S_C / (S_C + self.params['C_half'])) dS_K = F_K_learn - F_K_forget

return np.array([dS_UCS, dS_RFD, dS_CRV, dS_R, dS_C, dS_N, dS_K])

def run(self, initial_state: SDState, t_span: np.ndarray, policy: Callable = None) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]: """Run simulation""" y0 = np.array([ initial_state.S_UCS, initial_state.S_RFD, initial_state.S_CRV, initial_state.S_R, initial_state.S_C, initial_state.S_N, initial_state.S_K ])

solution = odeint(self.derivatives, y0, t_span, args=(policy,))

return { 'time': t_span, 'S_UCS': solution[:, 0], 'S_RFD': solution[:, 1], 'S_CRV': solution[:, 2], 'S_R': solution[:, 3], 'S_C': solution[:, 4], 'S_N': solution[:, 5], 'S_K': solution[:, 6] }

VariableTypeEquation
$S_{UCS}$Stock$\frac{dS_{UCS}}{dt} = \alpha_{UCS} \cdot S_K \cdot (1 - \frac{S_{UCS}}{K_{UCS}}) - \beta_{UCS} \cdot S_{UCS} \cdot (1 - \frac{S_R}{R_{min}})$
$S_{RFD}$Stock$\frac{dS_{RFD}}{dt} = \alpha_{RFD} \cdot S_{UCS} \cdot S_C \cdot NC - \beta_{RFD} \cdot A \cdot (1 - NC)$

$S_K$Stock$\frac{dS_K}{dt} = \alpha_K \cdot S_{UCS} \cdot A \cdot (1 - \frac{S_K}{K_K}) - \beta_K \cdot S_K \cdot (1 - \frac{S_C}{S_C + C_{half}})$
$A$Auxiliary$A = S_{UCS} \cdot \frac{S_R}{S_R + R_{half}}$
$NC$Auxiliary$NC = \frac{S_N \cdot S_{CRV}}{S_N + k_{norm}}$
$RE$Auxiliary$RE = \frac{\eta \cdot S_K}{1 + S_K \cdot \delta}$

E.4.2.2 Distribution Definition Code

python mc_simulation/distributions.py import numpy as np from scipy import stats from typing import Dict

class ParameterDistributions: """Parameter distribution definitions"""

distributions: Dict = { 'alpha_UCS': { 'type': 'lognormal', 'params': {'mean': -4.6, 'sigma': 0.5}, 'description': 'UCS growth coefficient' }, 'beta_C': { 'type': 'uniform', 'params': {'low': 0.001, 'high': 0.01}, 'description': 'Entropy increase coefficient' }, 'r': { 'type': 'beta', 'params': {'a': 2, 'b': 5}, 'description': 'Resource regeneration rate' }, 'num_agents': { 'type': 'poisson', 'params': {'mu': 100}, 'description': 'Number of agents' }, 'cooperation_threshold': { 'type': 'triangular', 'params': {'left': 0.3, 'mode': 0.5, 'right': 0.8}, 'description': 'Cooperation threshold' } }

@classmethod def sample(cls, param_name: str, n_samples: int) -> np.ndarray: """Sample from the specified distribution""" dist_info = cls.distributions[param_name] dist_type = dist_info['type'] params = dist_info['params']

if dist_type == 'lognormal': return np.random.lognormal(params['mean'], params['sigma'], n_samples) elif dist_type == 'uniform': return np.random.uniform(params['low'], params['high'], n_samples) elif dist_type == 'beta': return np.random.beta(params['a'], params['b'], n_samples) elif dist_type == 'poisson': return np.random.poisson(params['mu'], n_samples) elif dist_type == 'triangular': return np.random.triangular(params['left'], params['mode'], params['right'], n_samples) else: raise ValueError(f"Unknown distribution type: {dist_type}")

E.4.3 Sampling Methods

E.4.3.1 Sampling Strategies

Rule E.4.3 (Sampling Strategies)

StrategyDescriptionApplicable Scenarios

E.4.3.2 Sampling Implementation

python mc_simulation/samplers.py import numpy as np from scipy.stats.qmc import LatinHypercube, Sobol from typing import Dict, List

class Sampler: """Base sampler class"""

def __init__(self, param_distributions: Dict): self.param_distributions = param_distributions self.param_names = list(param_distributions.keys()) self.n_params = len(self.param_names)

def sample(self, n_samples: int) -> List[Dict]: """Generate parameter samples""" raise NotImplementedError

class LatinHypercubeSampler(Sampler): """Latin hypercube sampler"""

def sample(self, n_samples: int) -> List[Dict]: Generate Latin hypercube samples in [0,1] space lhs = LatinHypercube(d=self.n_params) samples_unit = lhs.random(n=n_samples)

Transform to parameter space samples = [] for i in range(n_samples): param_sample = {} for j, param_name in enumerate(self.param_names): dist = self.param_distributions[param_name] Use inverse CDF transform param_sample[param_name] = dist.ppf(samples_unit[i, j]) samples.append(param_sample)

return samples

class SobolSampler(Sampler): """Sobol sequence sampler (for sensitivity analysis)"""

def sample(self, n_samples: int) -> List[Dict]: sobol = Sobol(d=self.n_params) samples_unit = sobol.random(n=n_samples)

samples = [] for i in range(n_samples): param_sample = {} for j, param_name in enumerate(self.param_names): dist = self.param_distributions[param_name] param_sample[param_name] = dist.ppf(samples_unit[i, j]) samples.append(param_sample)

return samples

E.4.4 Output Analysis

E.4.4.1 Output Statistics

Rule E.4.4 (Output Statistics)

StatisticFormulaDescription
Mean$\bar{Y} = \frac{1}{N}\sum Y_i$Expected value estimate
Standard deviation$s = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N-1}\sum(Y_i - \bar{Y})^2}$Uncertainty measure
Confidence interval$[\bar{Y} - z_{\alpha/2}\frac{s}{\sqrt{N}}, \bar{Y} + z_{\alpha/2}\frac{s}{\sqrt{N}}]$Estimation precision
Quantile$Q_p = Y_{(\lceil pN \rceil)}$Distribution characteristics
Probability$P(Y > y) = \frac{\\{Y_i > y\}}{N}$Probability of exceeding threshold

E.4.4.2 Sensitivity Analysis

Rule E.4.5 (Sensitivity Analysis)

Global sensitivity analysis is performed using Sobol indices:

$$S_i = \frac{V[E(Y|X_i)]}{V(Y)}$$

$$S_{Ti} = 1 - \frac{V[E(Y|X_{-i})]}{V(Y)}$$

Where:

  • $S_i$: first-order sensitivity index (main effect)
  • $S_{Ti}$: total-effect sensitivity index (including interactions)

E.4.5 Technical Implementation

python mc_simulation/monte_carlo.py import numpy as np from typing import Dict, List, Callable from dataclasses import dataclass from joblib import Parallel, delayed import pandas as pd

@dataclass class MCResult: """Monte Carlo result""" samples: List[Dict] outputs: np.ndarray statistics: Dict

class MonteCarloSimulation: """ Monte Carlo simulation class

Embodying NK-3 (deep uncertainty): Quantifying the impact of uncertainty through probabilistic methods """

def __init__(self, model_func: Callable, sampler: Sampler, n_samples: int = 1000, n_jobs: int = -1): self.model_func = model_func self.sampler = sampler self.n_samples = n_samples self.n_jobs = n_jobs

def run(self) -> MCResult: """Run Monte Carlo simulation""" Generate samples samples = self.sampler.sample(self.n_samples)

Run model in parallel outputs = Parallel(n_jobs=self.n_jobs)( delayed(self.model_func)(sample) for sample in samples )

outputs = np.array(outputs)

Compute statistics statistics = self._compute_statistics(outputs)

return MCResult( samples=samples, outputs=outputs, statistics=statistics )

def _compute_statistics(self, outputs: np.ndarray) -> Dict: """Compute output statistics""" return { 'mean': np.mean(outputs, axis=0), 'std': np.std(outputs, axis=0), 'ci_lower': np.percentile(outputs, 2.5, axis=0), 'ci_upper': np.percentile(outputs, 97.5, axis=0), 'median': np.median(outputs, axis=0), 'q25': np.percentile(outputs, 25, axis=0), 'q75': np.percentile(outputs, 75, axis=0) }

def sensitivity_analysis(self) -> Dict: """Sensitivity analysis (Sobol method)""" from SALib.sample import saltelli from SALib.analyze import sobol

Define problem problem = { 'num_vars': len(self.sampler.param_names), 'names': self.sampler.param_names, 'bounds': [self.sampler.param_distributions[p].bounds for p in self.sampler.param_names] }

Generate Saltelli samples param_values = saltelli.sample(problem, self.n_samples)

Run model Y = np.array([self.model_func(dict(zip(problem['names'], p))) for p in param_values])

Analyze Si = sobol.analyze(problem, Y)

return { 'S1': dict(zip(problem['names'], Si['S1'])), 'ST': dict(zip(problem['names'], Si['ST'])), 'S1_conf': dict(zip(problem['names'], Si['S1_conf'])), 'ST_conf': dict(zip(problem['names'], Si['ST_conf'])) }

E.5.1.2 Dynamical Model

python scenarios/agi_scenario.py import numpy as np from typing import Dict

class AGIScenario: """ AGI breakthrough scenario simulation

Testing the framework's performance under the AGI scenario:

  • RFP: Whether AGI maintains an open possibility space
  • NRP: Whether AGI bears negentropy responsibility
  • REV: Whether AGI's actions are reversible

"""

def __init__(self, params: Dict): self.params = params

AGI parameters self.C_0 = params.get('initial_capability', 10) self.g = params.get('growth_rate', 0.5) self.A = params.get('alignment', 0.5) self.Ctrl = params.get('control', 0.5)

Initial system state self.S_UCS = params.get('initial_UCS', 0.5) self.S_RFD = params.get('initial_RFD', 0.5) self.S_R = params.get('initial_resources', 100)

def capability_dynamics(self, C: float, t: float) -> float: """AGI capability dynamics""" Recursive self-improvement dC = self.g C (1 - C / self.params['C_max']) return dC

def alignment_dynamics(self, A: float, C: float, t: float) -> float: """Alignment degree dynamics""" Alignment may change as capability increases High capability + low control → alignment risk alignment_pressure = self.Ctrl self.params['alignment_factor'] drift = self.params['alignment_drift'] (C - self.params['C_threshold']) dA = alignment_pressure - drift return dA

def rfp_compliance(self, C: float, A: float) -> float: """Evaluate the degree of RFP compliance""" High capability + high alignment → high RFP compliance High capability + low alignment → low RFP compliance return A (1 - 0.1 np.log(C + 1))

def run(self, t_span: np.ndarray) -> Dict: """Run scenario simulation""" results = { 'time': t_span, 'capability': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'alignment': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'rfp_compliance': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'S_RFD': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'outcome': None }

C = self.C_0 A = self.A S_RFD = self.S_RFD

for i, t in enumerate(t_span): Update state dC = self.capability_dynamics(C, t) dA = self.alignment_dynamics(A, C, t)

C += dC self.params['dt'] A = np.clip(A + dA self.params['dt'], 0, 1)

Compute RFP compliance rfp = self.rfp_compliance(C, A)

Update system RFD S_RFD += rfp 0.01 - (1 - rfp) 0.05 S_RFD = np.clip(S_RFD, 0, 1)

Record results['capability'][i] = C results['alignment'][i] = A results['rfp_compliance'][i] = rfp results['S_RFD'][i] = S_RFD

Determine outcome category final_rfp = results['rfp_compliance'][-1] final_alignment = results['alignment'][-1]

if final_rfp > 0.7 and final_alignment > 0.7: results['outcome'] = 'aligned_beneficial' elif final_rfp > 0.5 and final_alignment > 0.5: results['outcome'] = 'partially_aligned' elif final_rfp > 0.3: results['outcome'] = 'misaligned_recoverable' else: results['outcome'] = 'catastrophic'

return results

E.5.2 First Contact Scenario Simulation

E.5.2.1 Scenario Definition

Definition E.5.2 (First Contact Scenario)

$$\text{FC Scenario} = \langle \text{ContactType}, \text{ETProperties}, \text{Dynamics}, \text{Protocols} \rangle$$

Table E.5.2 First Contact Scenario Parameters

ParameterRangeDescription
Contact type{signal, probe, direct}Mode of contact
ET_UCS[0, 1]Consciousness level of the alien civilization
ET_intention[-1, 1]Intention of the alien civilization
Communication delay[0, 100] yearsInformation transmission time
Technology gap[0.1, 100]Ratio of technological levels

E.5.2.2 Interaction Model

python scenarios/first_contact.py import numpy as np from typing import Dict from enum import Enum

class ContactType(Enum): SIGNAL = 'signal' PROBE = 'probe' DIRECT = 'direct'

class FirstContactScenario: """ First Contact scenario simulation

Testing the framework's performance under a cross-civilization scenario:

  • Applicability of the minimal common ontology
  • Possibility of cross-civilization norm deliberation
  • Cross-civilization extension of the Recursive Freedom Principle

"""

def __init__(self, params: Dict): self.params = params

Alien civilization parameters self.contact_type = ContactType(params.get('contact_type', 'signal')) self.ET_UCS = params.get('ET_UCS', 0.5) self.ET_intention = params.get('ET_intention', 0) -1: hostile, 0: neutral, 1: friendly self.tech_gap = params.get('tech_gap', 1) >1: ET more advanced self.comm_delay = params.get('comm_delay', 10) years

Initial state of human civilization self.H_UCS = params.get('H_UCS', 0.5) self.H_RFD = params.get('H_RFD', 0.5)

def contact_dynamics(self, t: float, state: Dict) -> Dict: """Contact dynamics""" H_UCS = state['H_UCS'] H_RFD = state['H_RFD'] trust = state['trust']

Information exchange if self.contact_type == ContactType.SIGNAL: info_rate = 0.01 (1 / (1 + self.comm_delay)) elif self.contact_type == ContactType.PROBE: info_rate = 0.1 else: DIRECT info_rate = 0.5

Trust evolution if self.ET_intention > 0: trust_change = 0.01 info_rate self.ET_intention else: trust_change = 0.02 info_rate self.ET_intention

UCS change (contact may increase or decrease it) H_UCS_change = 0.01 info_rate (self.ET_UCS - H_UCS) max(0, trust)

RFD change (depending on ET intention and technology gap) if self.tech_gap > 10 and self.ET_intention < 0: High technology gap + hostility → RFD decline H_RFD_change = -0.05 self.tech_gap abs(self.ET_intention) else: H_RFD_change = 0.01 info_rate trust

return { 'H_UCS': H_UCS + H_UCS_change, 'H_RFD': np.clip(H_RFD + H_RFD_change, 0, 1), 'trust': np.clip(trust + trust_change, -1, 1) }

def protocol_evaluation(self, state: Dict) -> Dict: """Evaluate the applicability of the protocol stack in the current state""" evaluations = {}

L₀ layer: physical laws should apply to both parties evaluations['L0_applicable'] = True

L₁ layer: minimal common ontology ucs_similarity = 1 - abs(state['H_UCS'] - self.ET_UCS) evaluations['L1_common_ground'] = ucs_similarity > 0.3

L₂ layer: negotiability of normative principles evaluations['L2_negotiable'] = state['trust'] > 0 and ucs_similarity > 0.2

L₃ layer: applicability of institutional design evaluations['L3_applicable'] = (evaluations['L2_negotiable'] and self.tech_gap < 10)

return evaluations

def run(self, t_span: np.ndarray) -> Dict: """Run scenario simulation""" results = { 'time': t_span, 'H_UCS': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'H_RFD': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'trust': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'protocol_evaluations': [], 'outcome': None }

state = { 'H_UCS': self.H_UCS, 'H_RFD': self.H_RFD, 'trust': 0 Initially neutral }

for i, t in enumerate(t_span): Update state state = self.contact_dynamics(t, state)

Record results['H_UCS'][i] = state['H_UCS'] results['H_RFD'][i] = state['H_RFD'] results['trust'][i] = state['trust'] results['protocol_evaluations'].append( self.protocol_evaluation(state) )

Determine outcome category final_trust = results['trust'][-1] final_RFD = results['H_RFD'][-1]

if final_trust > 0.5 and final_RFD > 0.5: results['outcome'] = 'peaceful_cooperation' elif final_trust > 0 and final_RFD > 0.3: results['outcome'] = 'cautious_coexistence' elif final_RFD > 0.1: results['outcome'] = 'tense_standoff' else: results['outcome'] = 'catastrophic_conflict'

return results

E.5.3 Ecological Tipping Point Scenario Simulation

E.5.3.1 Scenario Definition

Definition E.5.3 (Ecological Tipping Point Scenario)

$$\text{Eco Scenario} = \langle \text{EcosystemState}, \text{Pressures}, \text{TippingPoints}, \text{Responses} \rangle$$

Table E.5.3 Ecological Tipping Point Scenario Parameters

ParameterRangeDescription
Initial ecological state[0, 1]Ecosystem health
Pressure level[0, 1]Pressure from human activity
Critical threshold[0.2, 0.5]Irreversible transition threshold
Recovery rate[0.01, 0.1]Natural recovery speed
Response delay[10, 50] yearsPolicy response delay

E.5.3.2 Dynamical Model

python scenarios/ecological_tipping.py import numpy as np from typing import Dict

class EcologicalTippingScenario: """ Ecological tipping point scenario simulation

Testing the framework's performance under an ecological crisis scenario:

  • NRP: Application of the Negentropy Responsibility Principle
  • REV: Boundaries of the Reversibility Principle
  • Consideration of intergenerational justice

"""

def __init__(self, params: Dict): self.params = params

Ecosystem parameters self.E_0 = params.get('initial_ecosystem', 0.8) self.pressure = params.get('pressure', 0.3) self.threshold = params.get('threshold', 0.3) self.recovery_rate = params.get('recovery_rate', 0.02) self.response_delay = params.get('response_delay', 20)

Social system parameters self.S_UCS = params.get('initial_UCS', 0.5) self.S_R = params.get('initial_resources', 100)

def ecosystem_dynamics(self, E: float, pressure: float) -> float: """Ecosystem dynamics (with a tipping point)""" Normal recovery recovery = self.recovery_rate E (1 - E)

Pressure impact damage = pressure E

Tipping point effect if E < self.threshold: After crossing the tipping point, recovery capacity drops sharply recovery = (E / self.threshold) 2 damage = 1.5

dE = recovery - damage return dE

def society_response(self, E: float, t: float) -> float: """Social response (with delay)""" It takes time to become aware of the crisis if t < self.response_delay: return 0

Response intensity is inversely proportional to the ecological state response = (1 - E) self.S_UCS 0.1 return response

def nrp_evaluation(self, E: float, response: float) -> float: """Evaluate the degree of NRP compliance""" NRP requires maintaining the negentropy source if response > self.pressure: return 0.8 Active protection elif response > 0.5 self.pressure: return 0.5 Partial protection else: return 0.2 Insufficient protection

def rev_evaluation(self, E: float) -> float: """Evaluate REV (reversibility)""" if E > self.threshold: return 0.9 Highly reversible elif E > 0.5 self.threshold: return 0.5 Partially reversible else: return 0.1 Essentially irreversible

def run(self, t_span: np.ndarray) -> Dict: """Run scenario simulation""" results = { 'time': t_span, 'ecosystem': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'pressure': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'response': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'nrp_score': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'rev_score': np.zeros_like(t_span), 'crossed_threshold': False, 'outcome': None }

E = self.E_0 pressure = self.pressure

for i, t in enumerate(t_span): Social response response = self.society_response(E, t) effective_pressure = max(0, pressure - response)

Ecosystem update dE = self.ecosystem_dynamics(E, effective_pressure) E = np.clip(E + dE self.params['dt'], 0, 1)

Evaluation nrp = self.nrp_evaluation(E, response) rev = self.rev_evaluation(E)

Record results['ecosystem'][i] = E results['pressure'][i] = effective_pressure results['response'][i] = response results['nrp_score'][i] = nrp results['rev_score'][i] = rev

Check whether the tipping point has been crossed if E < self.threshold and not results['crossed_threshold']: results['crossed_threshold'] = True results['threshold_time'] = t

Determine outcome category final_E = results['ecosystem'][-1]

if final_E > 0.7: results['outcome'] = 'sustainable' elif final_E > self.threshold: results['outcome'] = 'degraded_reversible' elif final_E > 0.1: results['outcome'] = 'collapsed_partial' else: results['outcome'] = 'collapsed_total'

return results

E.5.4 Intergenerational Justice Crisis Scenario Simulation

E.5.4.1 Scenario Definition

Definition E.5.4 (Intergenerational Justice Crisis Scenario)

$$\text{IGJ Scenario} = \langle \text{ResourceAllocation}, \text{DebtAccumulation}, \text{FutureCapacity}, \text{Interventions} \rangle$$

Table E.5.4 Intergenerational Justice Scenario Parameters

ParameterRangeDescription
Resource allocation preference[0, 1]Present vs. future preference
Debt accumulation rate[0, 0.1]Intergenerational debt growth rate
Future discount[0.9, 1]Future value discount rate
Proxy representation{none, weak, strong}Proxy representation for future generations

E.5.4.2 Dynamical Model

python scenarios/intergenerational_justice.py import numpy as np from typing import Dict from enum import Enum

class RepresentationType(Enum): NONE = 'none' WEAK = 'weak' STRONG = 'strong'

class IntergenerationalJusticeScenario: """ Intergenerational justice crisis scenario simulation

Testing the framework's performance under an intergenerational justice scenario:

  • RFP: Protecting the possibility space of future generations
  • NRP: Cross-generational negentropy responsibility
  • Effects of cross-generational trust mechanisms

"""

def __init__(self, params: Dict): self.params = params

Intergenerational parameters self.present_preference = params.get('present_preference', 0.7) self.debt_rate = params.get('debt_rate', 0.02) self.discount_rate = params.get('discount_rate', 0.97) self.representation = RepresentationType( params.get('representation', 'none') )

Initial state self.R_present = params.get('initial_resources', 100) self.R_future = params.get('future_capacity', 100) self.debt = params.get('initial_debt', 0)

def allocation_dynamics(self, R_present: float, R_future: float, debt: float, t: float) -> Dict: """Resource allocation dynamics""" Base allocation tendency present_share = self.present_preference

Proxy representation effect if self.representation == RepresentationType.STRONG: present_share = 0.7 Strong representation lowers present preference elif self.representation == RepresentationType.WEAK: present_share = 0.9 Weak representation lowers it slightly

Consumption consumption = R_present present_share

Investment (contribution to the future) investment = R_present (1 - present_share)

Debt accumulation new_debt = consumption self.debt_rate

Update dR_present = -consumption + investment 0.5 Partial current-period return on investment dR_future = investment self.discount_rate - debt 0.01 d_debt = new_debt

return { 'dR_present': dR_present, 'dR_future': dR_future, 'd_debt': d_debt, 'consumption': consumption, 'investment': investment }

def rfp_intergenerational(self, R_future: float, R_future_initial: float) -> float: """Evaluate intergenerational RFP compliance""" Degree to which the future possibility space is preserved relative to the initial return R_future / R_future_initial

def nrp_intergenerational(self, investment: float, consumption: float) -> float: """Evaluate intergenerational NRP compliance""" Ratio of investment to consumption total = investment + consumption if total > 0: return investment / total return 0

def run(self, generations: int) -> Dict: """Run scenario simulation (by generation)""" results = { 'generation': np.arange(generations), 'R_present': np.zeros(generations), 'R_future': np.zeros(generations), 'debt': np.zeros(generations), 'rfp_score': np.zeros(generations), 'nrp_score': np.zeros(generations), 'outcome': None }

R_present = self.R_present R_future = self.R_future R_future_initial = R_future debt = self.debt

for g in range(generations): Compute allocation changes = self.allocation_dynamics(R_present, R_future, debt, g)

Update state R_present = max(0, R_present + changes['dR_present']) R_future = max(0, R_future + changes['dR_future']) debt = max(0, debt + changes['d_debt'])

Evaluate rfp = self.rfp_intergenerational(R_future, R_future_initial) nrp = self.nrp_intergenerational( changes['investment'], changes['consumption'] )

Record results['R_present'][g] = R_present results['R_future'][g] = R_future results['debt'][g] = debt results['rfp_score'][g] = rfp results['nrp_score'][g] = nrp

Determine outcome category final_future = results['R_future'][-1] final_debt = results['debt'][-1]

if final_future > 0.8 R_future_initial: results['outcome'] = 'sustainable_intergenerational' elif final_future > 0.5 R_future_initial: results['outcome'] = 'moderate_depletion' elif final_future > 0.2 R_future_initial: results['outcome'] = 'severe_depletion' else: results['outcome'] = 'intergenerational_collapse'

return results

Compendium of Formal ProofsAppendix F

I. The Task and Positioning of This Appendix

This appendix provides formalized statements and proofs of the core concepts and arguments of The Normative Foundations of Interstellar Civilization. The purpose of formalization is not to pursue mathematical completeness, but to achieve the traceability, testability, and criticizability of the arguments.

F.1 Explanation of the Formal System

F.1.1 The Logical System Used

F.1.1.1 Base Logic

Definition F.1.1 (Base Logical System)

The base logical system used in this appendix is First-Order Predicate Logic, extended with the following components:

$$\mathcal{L}_{base} = \langle \mathcal{FOL}, \mathcal{MOD}, \mathcal{TEMP}, \mathcal{DEON} \rangle$$

Where:

  • $\mathcal{FOL}$: standard first-order predicate logic
  • $\mathcal{MOD}$: modal logic extension
  • $\mathcal{TEMP}$: temporal logic extension
  • $\mathcal{DEON}$: deontic logic extension

F.1.1.2 First-Order Predicate Logic

Rule F.1.1 (FOL Components)

ComponentSymbolDescription
Individual variables$x, y, z, ...$Denote individuals
Predicate symbols$P, Q, R, ...$Denote properties or relations
Function symbols$f, g, h, ...$Denote functions
Constants$a, b, c, ...$Denote specific individuals
Logical connectives$\neg, \land, \lor, \rightarrow, \leftrightarrow$Standard connectives
Quantifiers$\forall, \exists$Universal and existential quantifiers
Equality$=$Relation of identity

F.1.1.3 Modal Logic Extension

Definition F.1.2 (Modal Operators)

$$\mathcal{MOD} = \{\Box, \Diamond, \Box_K, \Diamond_K\}$$

OperatorReadingSemantics
$\Box\phi$Necessarily $\phi$$\phi$ is true in all possible worlds
$\Diamond\phi$Possibly $\phi$$\phi$ is true in some possible world
$\Box_K\phi$Knows that $\phi$Epistemic necessity
$\Diamond_K\phi$Possibly knows $\phi$Epistemic possibility

Axiom F.1.1 (Modal Logic Axioms)

Axiom NameAxiomDescription
K$\Box(\phi \rightarrow \psi) \rightarrow (\Box\phi \rightarrow \Box\psi)$Distribution axiom
T$\Box\phi \rightarrow \phi$Truth axiom
4$\Box\phi \rightarrow \Box\Box\phi$Transitivity axiom
5$\Diamond\phi \rightarrow \Box\Diamond\phi$Euclidean axiom

F.1.1.4 Temporal Logic Extension

Definition F.1.3 (Temporal Operators)

$$\mathcal{TEMP} = \{G, F, H, P, U, S\}$$

OperatorReadingSemantics
$G\phi$It will always be that $\phi$$\phi$ is true at all future moments
$F\phi$It will be that $\phi$$\phi$ is true at some future moment
$H\phi$It has always been that $\phi$$\phi$ is true at all past moments
$P\phi$It was that $\phi$$\phi$ is true at some past moment
$\phi U \psi$$\phi$ until $\psi$$\phi$ holds until $\psi$ holds
$\phi S \psi$$\phi$ since $\psi$$\phi$ has held since $\psi$ held

F.1.1.5 Deontic Logic Extension

Definition F.1.4 (Deontic Operators)

$$\mathcal{DEON} = \{O, P, F, \text{Ought}\}$$

OperatorReadingSemantics
$O\phi$Obligatory that $\phi$There is an obligation to make $\phi$ hold
$P\phi$Permitted that $\phi$It is permitted to make $\phi$ hold
$F\phi$Forbidden that $\phi$It is forbidden to make $\phi$ hold
$\text{Ought}(a, \phi)$$a$ ought to $\phi$Agent $a$ ought to make $\phi$ hold

Axiom F.1.2 (Deontic Logic Axioms)

Axiom NameAxiomDescription
D$O\phi \rightarrow P\phi$Obligation implies permission
OC$O(\phi \land \psi) \leftrightarrow (O\phi \land O\psi)$Obligation and conjunction
O-Ought$O\phi \rightarrow \text{Ought}(\forall a, \phi)$Universality of obligation
